title: The tribes
hookLine: life was held together by tribe and clan, for protection and for honor
last: A LAND OF WELLS AND WORDS.

cards: Who are your people? In Mecca before Islam, the answer could decide whether you lived. Ask a man his name and he would give you a chain: son of this one, of that clan, of that tribe.
There was no police force and no state. Your clan was your protection. Harm one of its members and the whole clan answered.
Lose your clan and you stood alone in the open. Today's word is the thing that held that world together.

teach.b: The word is qabilah: a tribe. As the sirah describes it, a tribe was made of clans, and clans of families, nested like rooms in a house.
In Mecca the tribe was Quraysh, and among its clans was Banu Hashim, the clan the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would be born into. Belonging gave you honor, a name to stand behind, and above all protection.
The custom of blood vengeance meant an attack on one person was an attack on the clan. That threat kept people safe. It also kept feuds burning.

The protective side matters later: the sirah tells how the Prophet's uncle Abu Talib, of the same clan, sheltered him when others turned hostile. But tribal loyalty could also mean standing by your own, right or wrong.

teach.h: HELP YOUR BROTHER, OPPRESSOR OR OPPRESSED.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet says: help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. The companions were puzzled. Helping the oppressed, yes.
But how do you help an oppressor? By stopping him from oppressing, he answered. Some readers hear in the first half an echo of an old desert saying, turned inside out by the second.
Loyalty stays. Its job changes. Surah forty-nine uses this very word, in the plural.

teach.h: TRIBES, THAT YE MAY KNOW ONE ANOTHER.
teach.b: Pickthall translates: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another." Tribes are not erased. They are given a purpose.

teach.h: THE NOBLEST OF YOU IS THE BEST IN CONDUCT.
teach.b: And the verse goes on, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct." In a world that measured honor by lineage, that turned the ladder sideways. Your line still names you.

how: Qur'an 49:13 is recited in sermons and classes on family, race and belonging, and the hadith about helping an oppressor by stopping him is taught alongside it.

o: a merchant caravan crossing the desert together
a tribe: clans and families bound for protection
a council of elders that ruled the whole city

p: tribes, that ye may know one another

s: the Qur'an tells people to abandon their tribes
49:13 keeps tribes and gives them a purpose: to know one another.
in 49:13 the noblest is the best in conduct
not the one with the best lineage.
in the hadith, helping an oppressor means standing with him
it means stopping him from oppressing.

games.q: you're a companion. the Prophet ﷺ says: help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. you ask how anyone helps an oppressor. what does he answer?
o: stand with him: family comes first.
leave him to face what's coming.
games.why: by stopping him. the old loyalty stays, but its job changes. Sahih al-Bukhari reports it.

practice: Bring to mind your people: family by blood, the ones you chose, or a community that took you in, and let one face come close, someone who stood behind you when you were in trouble.
If you pray, you can thank Allah for them and ask good for them; if you don't, just say thank you silently, as if they could hear it.

wordCard.voice: Qabilah. A tribe: clans and families bound together for protection and honor. Surah forty-nine uses its plural: tribes, that you may know one another. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: tribe; its plural, qaba'il, is the word in 49:13.

carryVoice: Your line: belonging protected you. Tomorrow, poets at the fair. Until then.
